strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses an important challenge in generating videos that maintain scene consistency while following precise camera trajectories over extended sequences

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple metrics, diverse datasets (DynPose-100K, RealEstate10K), and thorough ablation studies examining key design choices and components
Clear presentation and visualization: Well-structured methodology with helpful figures (3-5) explaining the framework, and convincing qualitative results across multiple scenarios (Figures 6-12)
Practical system design: The three-stage dynamic masking pipeline is carefully designed to separate static geometry from dynamic elements, preventing ghosting artifacts
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is primarily architectural integration of existing techniques (SLAM, spatio-temporal conditioning, optical flow detection, SAM2, CoTracker3) rather than fundamental innovation in any component

Significant computational efficiency concerns: Table 10 reveals 9+ minutes inference time for 4-frame generation vs. 1-3 seconds for baselines—a critical limitation unresolved by proposed DepthAnything v3 replacement

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Limited direct comparison with other recent geometry-grounded or multi-frame conditioned camera-controllable video generation methods; primary baseline is DFoT with sometimes modest improvements

Purely empirical analysis: No theoretical justification for why dual conditioning works or investigation into what the 3D scene memory learns differently from simple geometry conditioning
Problematic ablation findings: Massive performance drops without dynamic masking (Table 6) raise concerns about method robustness and whether such complex engineering is necessary

Limited novelty scope: While addressing a relevant problem, the advances are primarily incremental refinements of spatio-temporal conditioning rather than transformative contributions to video generation
